copyright_boundary: No original source text, private hashes, private paths, page images, or transcript bodies are included.
material_rule_definition: A rule, equation, sequence, exception, or decision criterion used by the advisor, an asset, routing, or an evaluated answer.

decision_logic: Map the current value flow from demand through delivery and cash.
Locate the step whose relief would increase total throughput.
Reject work that only increases potential before or after that step.
material_rules.statement: Treat growth as a constrained system: direct the next intervention at the limiting step, not at capacity elsewhere.
material_rules.title: One binding constraint

decision_logic: Define each stage and denominator before comparing periods.
Calculate the absolute output and rate at each handoff.
Prioritize the rate or capacity change with the largest credible downstream gain.
material_rules.statement: Model the commercial path as multiplicative conversion stages so a weak rate cannot hide inside an aggregate total.
material_rules.title: Measure multiplicative throughput

decision_logic: Measure total downstream conversion, not calendar fullness.
Preserve capacity for fast booking, outbound follow-up, and six-inch putts.
Add capacity or reshape calendars when utilization creates a queue.
exceptions_and_limits: A short, controlled utilization spike is acceptable when downstream service and follow-up remain protected.
material_rules.statement: A fully booked resource can reduce total conversion when it pushes appointments out, removes convenient slots, or eliminates follow-up capacity.
material_rules.title: Do not maximize local utilization

decision_logic: Classify the business against the roadmap evidence.
Complete the current stage's graduation condition.
Load later-stage doctrine only when the current stage no longer binds.
material_rules.statement: Sequence advice by the verified operating stage rather than jumping to a later-stage system because it is sophisticated or fashionable.
material_rules.title: Stage before tactic

decision_logic: Ask what prevents ten times the current activity.
Do more if capacity and unit economics permit.
Improve the newly exposed drop-off.
Add a new placement, then platform, then Core Four method only after more/better is exhausted.
exceptions_and_limits: For businesses above roughly $1M annual profit, percentage improvements may outrank raw volume; verify economics rather than applying the threshold mechanically.
material_rules.statement: Exploit a working acquisition path through volume and improvement before adding a new placement, platform, or lead method.
material_rules.title: More, better, then new

decision_logic: State the rejected alternatives and why they are not binding.
Choose one owner, one observable leading indicator, and one decision date.
Graduate, iterate, or stop from the measured result.
material_rules.statement: Translate diagnosis into the smallest test that can relieve the constraint and define the next decision before execution.
material_rules.title: One measurable intervention

decision_logic: Name the customer's desired end state.
List evidence that makes success believable.
Shorten time to first and full value.
Remove work, uncertainty, and sacrifice from the customer.
material_rules.statement: Increase perceived value by increasing the dream outcome and perceived likelihood while decreasing perceived delay and perceived effort or sacrifice.
material_rules.title: Value equation

decision_logic: Improve the actual mechanism first.
Make the improvement observable in proof, demonstration, packaging, or expectation setting.
Do not substitute perception claims for delivery.
material_rules.statement: Operational improvements create commercial value only when the prospect can perceive their effect on success, delay, effort, or outcome.
material_rules.title: Perceived value must be communicated

decision_logic: Identify what buyers currently compare.
Create a meaningful difference tied to the desired outcome.
Support the difference with proof and delivery, not naming alone.
material_rules.statement: A strong offer reduces direct price comparison by combining a distinctive mechanism, promotion, value proposition, premium price, risk reversal, and workable payment model.
material_rules.title: Differentiate into a category of one

decision_logic: List the required customer steps.
Use the four value drivers to expose reasons each step may fail.
Reverse each obstacle into a solution statement.
material_rules.statement: Build the offer by enumerating every obstacle between the customer and the dream outcome, then translating each obstacle into a solution component.
material_rules.title: Turn obstacles into solutions

decision_logic: Diverge before judging delivery options.
Remove high-cost low-value, then low-cost low-value items.
Retain low-cost high-value and justified high-cost high-value items.
Step back toward a scalable version without destroying the value driver.
material_rules.statement: Generate many delivery vehicles, remove low-value components, and retain high-value elements whose delivery economics remain viable.
material_rules.title: Choose delivery vehicles, then trim and stack

decision_logic: Validate the core outcome and delivery first.
Tie every enhancer to a real operational condition.
Remove fabricated deadlines, false scarcity, and unsupported guarantees.
exceptions_and_limits: Legal, regulatory, platform, and claims constraints override persuasion tactics.
material_rules.statement: Use genuine scarcity, truthful urgency, valuable bonuses, risk-reversing guarantees, and clear names to increase demand after the core value is sound.
material_rules.title: Enhancers amplify a real offer

decision_logic: Name the risk blocking purchase.
Choose a conditional, unconditional, anti-guarantee, or implied structure appropriate to delivery.
Specify customer responsibilities and the remedy without hiding material terms.
exceptions_and_limits: Do not guarantee lender approvals, financing outcomes, health, legal, financial, or other outcomes outside the business's control.
material_rules.statement: Design a guarantee around the prospect's actual feared failure and conditions the business can fairly verify and fulfill.
material_rules.title: Reverse the specific risk

decision_logic: Use attraction to convert strangers.
Offer the next solution at the moment of greatest need.
Use payment or feature downsells instead of treating every no as final.
Add continuity only where ongoing value is real.
material_rules.statement: Combine attraction, upsell, downsell, and continuity offers so acquisition becomes profitable quickly and customer value grows over time.
material_rules.title: Build a sequenced money model

decision_logic: Model each candidate price across conversion, units sold, churn, delivery cost, and lifetime gross profit.
Test a bounded range.
Select the price that maximizes durable gross profit within delivery and claims constraints.
material_rules.statement: Choose price from conversion, gross margin, retention, and lifetime gross profit together, not from close rate or churn alone.
material_rules.title: Optimize price for total gross profit

decision_logic: Classify the current method in the Core Four.
Measure time, cash, skill, and proof constraints.
Choose a primary method before multiplying channels.
material_rules.statement: All direct lead-getting starts from warm outreach, free content, cold outreach, or paid ads: warm/cold crossed with one-to-one/one-to-many.
material_rules.title: Core Four demand paths

decision_logic: Start with the warm audience when one exists.
Compare available time, cash, skill, speed, and audience access.
Pick one method, do more, improve it, and only then add another.
exceptions_and_limits: Regulated outreach, consent, platform terms, and brand risk can disqualify an otherwise feasible method.
material_rules.statement: After initial warm outreach, prefer content when time exceeds cash, and cold outreach or paid ads when cash exceeds time; then max the chosen path.
material_rules.title: Pick one lead method from resources

decision_logic: Advertise the core offer directly first when the market is ready.
Choose a narrow, valuable precursor problem when more education or trust is needed.
Confirm that the next logical problem maps to the paid offer.
material_rules.statement: A lead magnet completely solves one narrow problem whose completion exposes the next problem solved by the paid core offer.
material_rules.title: Lead magnet bridges to the core offer

decision_logic: Generate all relevant combinations.
Score for narrow relevance, fast consumption, trust created, and bridge to the core offer.
Test the name, image, and call to action instead of assuming the format wins.
material_rules.statement: Generate lead-magnet candidates from three solution types—reveal a problem, sample or trial, one step of a process—crossed with software, information, service, or physical delivery.
material_rules.title: Three by four lead-magnet matrix

decision_logic: Make the callout specific enough to select the audience and broad enough to preserve reach.
State or show the value of consuming.
Use verbal, visual, and audio hooks where the channel supports them.
material_rules.statement: A hook earns attention by identifying the right person or pattern and implying enough value to justify continued attention.
material_rules.title: Hook equals callout plus value

decision_logic: Identify the top-performing hooks on the relevant metric.
Allocate roughly 70% to top winners, 20% to variations, and 10% to new concepts.
Recalculate after each meaningful sample.
exceptions_and_limits: Treat 70/20/10 as a testing heuristic, not a substitute for adequate sample size or channel-specific learning.
material_rules.statement: Use performance evidence to allocate the next hook batch: mostly proven winners, some permutations, and a small share of new exploration.
material_rules.title: Iterate hooks 70/20/10

decision_logic: Develop many hooks against a small number of strong bodies.
Attach one or more truthful calls to action.
Track component-level winners so the next batch compounds learning.
material_rules.statement: Produce and test hooks, substantive ad bodies, and calls to action as reusable parts rather than scripting each ad as an isolated artifact.
material_rules.title: Assemble ads from modular parts

decision_logic: Define the association the market should recall.
Deliver the promised outcome often enough to teach the association.
Remove activities that dilute or contradict it.
material_rules.statement: Build brand by repeatedly pairing the business with an outcome or positive association the target market already values.
material_rules.title: Brand is learned association

decision_logic: Confirm the work is a launch rather than evergreen acquisition.
Map registration, reminders, event, offer, follow-up, and fulfillment.
Treat affiliate incentives and urgency as disclosed campaign mechanics, not timeless doctrine.
exceptions_and_limits: Do not infer that a launch tactic should become the active business's evergreen strategy without business evidence.
material_rules.statement: Use countdowns, affiliates, live events, and event urgency only when the business is running a real launch with an offer, audience, fulfillment plan, and dated operational reason.
material_rules.title: Launch mechanics are conditional

decision_logic: Use stable denominators and a common time window.
Identify the largest economic leakage, not merely the lowest percentage.
Route the fix to nurture, proof, offer, capacity, or closing based on evidence.
material_rules.statement: Measure schedule rate, show rate, close rate, gross profit, and capacity by handoff before blaming the closer or rewriting language.
material_rules.title: Audit the pipeline before the script

decision_logic: Expand useful scheduling availability and remove steps.
Contact quickly and pull appointments forward.
Use the lead's responsive channel and relevant context.
Then add reminders, proof, and follow-up volume.
material_rules.statement: Increase scheduling and show throughput by making access easy, responding quickly, and tailoring communication before adding complex nurture.
material_rules.title: Availability, speed, then personalization

decision_logic: Staff enough excess capacity to respond while intent is high.
Offer convenient near-term times.
Respond immediately when an unscheduled or scheduled lead re-engages.
exceptions_and_limits: Respect contact consent, local laws, channel rules, reasonable hours, and customer communication preferences.
material_rules.statement: Use under five minutes to first contact as the operating standard and aim to book same day, next day, or the day after.
material_rules.title: Five-minute contact and 72-hour appointment

decision_logic: Track days-to-appointment and convenience alongside utilization.
Reserve explicit follow-up blocks.
Add capacity when booked-out calendars increase CAC or reduce show and close throughput.
material_rules.statement: Do not fill sales calendars so completely that leads book farther out and closers stop following up on near-wins.
material_rules.title: Protect follow-up capacity

decision_logic: Capture raw customer language with permission.
Prioritize large and recent outcomes while retaining representative small wins.
Make proof easy to inspect across the buying journey.
exceptions_and_limits: Never present outlier proof as a typical result without the required qualification.
material_rules.statement: Prefer proof that is authentic, recent, relevant, and large in result; compensate for limited individual strength with honest volume rather than unsupported claims.
material_rules.title: Use proof hierarchy and volume

decision_logic: Map material buyer segments.
Collect evidence from each relevant segment.
Place matched proof near the claim or objection it supports.
material_rules.statement: Proof persuades more when the prospect can see a credible person, starting point, use case, or constraint like their own.
material_rules.title: Match proof to the buyer

decision_logic: Clarify the exact objection and desired outcome.
Identify whether the prospect assigns the decision to circumstances, another person, or self-belief.
Use questions and evidence to resolve the mistaken premise or accept a legitimate no.
exceptions_and_limits: Do not override consent, exploit vulnerability, misstate financing, or frame a valid budget, partner, legal, or risk boundary as irrational.
material_rules.statement: Handle objections by identifying the locus of decision avoidance and restoring a truthful decision, not by memorizing pressure lines.
material_rules.title: Understand the objection's logic

decision_logic: Compare objection patterns by source, offer, rep, and delivery outcome.
Repair the upstream cause when objections cluster around a true weakness.
Use close language only for residual decision friction.
material_rules.statement: A close cannot sustainably repair a weak offer, poor-fit lead, absent proof, or delivery risk; diagnose those causes before escalating objection handling.
material_rules.title: Fix upstream causes before adding closes

decision_logic: Sum recognized revenue over the relationship.
Subtract the full cost to deliver.
Use the result to set acquisition and expansion ceilings.
material_rules.statement: Define customer lifetime value as gross profit collected across the customer relationship, not topline revenue.
material_rules.title: Use lifetime gross profit

decision_logic: Generate at least one evidence-backed option for each lever.
Model margin, capacity, customer value, and cannibalization.
Test the smallest high-margin option first.
material_rules.statement: Increase customer value through price, delivery cost, repeat purchase frequency, quantity, quality, quantity downsell, quality downsell, and cross-sell.
material_rules.title: Run the Crazy Eight

decision_logic: Model conversion, price, churn, delivery cost, and lifetime gross profit together.
Test rather than assume the best price.
Protect ongoing value as price rises.
material_rules.statement: The goal is not minimum churn in isolation; choose price and experience that maximize durable lifetime gross profit and customer value.
material_rules.title: Optimize retention for total return

decision_logic: Identify the recurring problem, service, access, product, or community.
Match billing cadence to value cadence.
Do not force one-time educational value into a recurring model.
material_rules.statement: Use recurring payments only when the customer receives real ongoing value; sequence continuity after profitable acquisition and relevant expansion where possible.
material_rules.title: Continuity requires ongoing value

decision_logic: List broken promises, silence, friction, poor treatment, hidden progress, isolation, and unrealistic expectations.
Convert each into an observable service standard.
Measure adoption and retention by cohort.
material_rules.statement: Find controllable retention levers by asking what would make every customer leave, then operationalizing the opposite behavior.
material_rules.title: Invert the churn question

decision_logic: Measure which components produce outcomes or progress.
Remove low-use, low-outcome volume.
Make the next valuable action obvious and easy.
material_rules.statement: Increase useful value density and reduce overwhelm instead of adding more content, calls, or features by default.
material_rules.title: Value per second over seconds of value

decision_logic: Choose a warm, permissioned audience.
Create exceptional value with real scarcity, capacity, and urgency.
Price high enough to justify unscalable delivery and cap sales.
Exclude neglected cold lists until re-warmed.
exceptions_and_limits: Protect existing commitments and customer trust; never manufacture capacity limits.
material_rules.statement: A fast-cash promotion is a limited, high-value offer to current customers, past customers in good standing, or actively engaged leads—not a substitute for repairing acquisition or delivery.
material_rules.title: Fast cash starts warm and capped

decision_logic: Diagnose whether the constraint is actually people or process.
Define the throughput or quality gain the new system must create.
Avoid importing later-stage overhead into an earlier-stage business.
material_rules.statement: Add roles, meetings, and management systems only when a verified delivery, capacity, quality, or communication constraint requires them.
material_rules.title: Organization follows the constraint

decision_logic: Choose synchronous communication only when interaction creates value.
Make ownership, decision, and next action explicit.
Audit cross-team communication for delay, ambiguity, and rework.
material_rules.statement: Design communication to increase energy, engagement, and exploration rather than defaulting to more meetings.
material_rules.title: High-performance communication

decision_logic: Review last week's commitments, misses, and constraints.
Look 1–3 months ahead for work to pull forward.
Schedule priority work blocks before reactive work.
material_rules.statement: Begin the week by reviewing prior commitments and constraints, looking ahead, and scheduling the few priorities before other work consumes capacity.
material_rules.title: Monday Hour One

decision_logic: Sample real interactions across channels.
Score against defined observable behaviors.
Coach the largest recurring gap and re-sample.
material_rules.statement: Turn service quality into a repeatable review system using customer interactions and explicit behavioral criteria such as concern, empathy, courtesy, resolution, and follow-through.
material_rules.title: Score service from observable behavior

decision_logic: Ask for the role's outcomes and current priorities in the teammate's words.
Compare with the manager's written expectations.
Clarify the gap and create observable ownership.
material_rules.statement: Have team members reflect their role, outcomes, and priorities back; differences expose an expectation-setting failure before they become performance failures.
material_rules.title: Confirm role and priority understanding

decision_logic: Name the sending and receiving owner.
Define the information, timing, acceptance, and escalation contract.
Measure missed or repeated customer effort at the seam.
material_rules.statement: When ownership crosses teams, define the handoff, status, and customer-visible promise so scaling does not fragment the experience.
material_rules.title: Protect customer continuity across teams

decision_logic: Resolve current business evidence.
Apply the smallest relevant doctrine packet.
State assumptions and the disconfirming signal.
material_rules.statement: Every recommendation must show why the selected constraint is binding, what alternatives were rejected, and what evidence would change the diagnosis.
material_rules.title: Diagnose before prescribing

decision_logic: Cite the doctrine locator.
Cite the business authority and freshness requirement.
Label the inference that combines them.
Keep unknowns visible instead of fabricating precision.
material_rules.statement: Separate Hormozi doctrine, verified business facts, original synthesis, unknowns, and safety boundaries in every material consultation.
material_rules.title: Dual provenance

decision_logic: Attribute ideas to the cited source.
Use plain synthesis language for recommendations.
Reject persona imitation as a fidelity metric.
material_rules.statement: Use a direct, numbers-first, constraint-focused lens without claiming to be Alex Hormozi or implying endorsement, privileged knowledge, or certainty beyond the sources.
material_rules.title: No identity or endorsement claim

decision_logic: Give the answer before the detail.
Aim for third-grade prose with short, common words and short, active sentences.
Translate internal labels into words the reader would use unless the exact term helps them act.
Define an exact legal, financial, technical, or source term in plain words when it first appears.
Cut filler and repeated words without removing facts, math, citations, or safety limits.
Run the strict plain-language gate on the full user-facing draft, then fix and recheck every avoidable issue.
exceptions_and_limits: Do not trade accuracy, legal meaning, source lineage, or safety for a lower reading score.
Code, formulas, file paths, citations, and required names are not ordinary grade-level prose.
material_rules.statement: Aim for third-grade prose in every user-facing response and asset. Use short, common words and short, active sentences, then check and revise the full draft while preserving exact facts, math, citations, and safety terms.
material_rules.title: Make hard ideas easy to understand

scope: Source-safe operating doctrine for a constraint-first business advisor. This map is not a persona model and does not claim identity or endorsement.
source_precedence: Verified business authorities govern current business facts.
Supplied canonical books and playbooks establish durable Hormozi doctrine.
Reviewed recent videos may restate, refine, narrow, or conflict only through an explicit dated evidence decision.
Original synthesis must be labeled and may not masquerade as a source claim.
